tldr: Heavy news cycle: three critical vulnerabilities under active exploitation (Zyxel GS1900 zero-day, Cisco's "Node2Shell" Brotli bug, a Barracuda ESG root chain), major breaches at blockchain-intel firm Chainalysis and French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa (~$133M), plus a Russian APT29 mobile spyware campaign. AI platforms and AI-offensive tooling are a recurring thread through both the incident list and the emerging threats below.

emerging.title: CERT-In flags "Crafty Falcon" autonomous AI attack chains hitting Indian banks, crypto firms
emerging.description: India's CERT-In is tracking a threat actor using public AI-offensive frameworks (ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI) to run full autonomous attack chains against BFSI and crypto firms, stealing keys/funds. Separately, a backdoored ARTEX Docker image gave unauthenticated root on 62 internet-facing consoles.

emerging.title: OpenAI's AI pipeline generates 948 working Linux root exploits in one run
emerging.description: An autonomous pipeline built on an unreleased OpenAI cyber model found and weaponized 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities in a single ~$1.2M run using 10+ novel exploitation techniques — a signal that AI-driven vulnerability research may outpace patch cycles.

items.title: Zyxel patch fails to stop zero-day hitting GS1900 switches
items.description: Zyxel's October fix for CVE-2026-7273 didn't block the real attack: researchers found ~1,000 GS1900 switches compromised via a separate zero-day (CVE-2026-107441, CVSS 8.8) delivering Jitterly/Sixzut malware.

items.title: Cisco's "Node2Shell" Brotli flaw under active exploitation across 19+ products
items.description: Cisco confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli library, hitting 19 Cisco products (dozens more under review) and Splunk. WatchGuard and SonicWall issued related patches/EOL warnings the same day.

items.title: Barracuda patches ESG flaw chain enabling unauthenticated root access
items.description: Barracuda fixed CVE-2026-116606 (auth bypass, CVSS 9.3) and CVE-2026-111560 (command injection, CVSS 8.6) in Email Security Gateway; chained, they give unauthenticated attackers root. Shared code affects five more Barracuda products.

items.title: Critical OpenSSH flaw lets attackers bypass auth on musl-based Linux
items.description: A crypt() quirk on Alpine Linux and other musl systems let attackers log into password-less, key-only accounts using a long dummy password on the first try. OpenSSH 10.6p2 and Alpine patches shipped Nov 5; no known exploitation yet.

items.title: Chainalysis breach exposes credentials for all users
items.description: The blockchain-analytics firm used by law enforcement and crypto regulators confirmed names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens were exposed for every user via an "offensive agentic" intrusion; KYT and login pages taken offline Nov 4.

items.title: French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms ~$133M cyber heist
items.description: Attackers breached a supplier to reach the bank's systems and moved funds to other institutions over several days starting Nov 2, converting some to crypto. Customer accounts/assets unaffected; some funds frozen.

items.title: Attackers target AI developer platforms for stolen model-access tokens
items.description: At least a dozen AI developer platforms breached in the past month, most recently WorkOS, Northflank, Trigger.dev and Chainstack (Oct 26-30), with attackers harvesting AI access keys for resale/LLM-jacking.

items.title: Supply-chain attack on OpsShield pushes rooted cPGuard update to ~2,950 servers
items.description: Attackers hijacked OpsShield's update CDN for ~70 minutes, shipping malicious cPGuard builds that opened hidden root shells on Linux hosting servers and copied ~7,900 customer account records.

items.title: Russia's APT29 runs mobile watering-hole campaign with reused spyware exploits
items.description: Sekoia details a Midnight Blizzard campaign hitting iOS/Android users via compromised Ukrainian, Bulgarian and political-party sites plus a hijacked analytics script (Plerdy), using the DarkSword kit and a Chrome/Qualcomm chain; CISA added CVE-2024-27834 to its KEV catalog Nov 4.

items.title: Cyberattack hits French blood bank's cold-storage systems
items.description: Attackers pushed EFS plasma freezer setpoints toward 110°C at three sites via a vulnerable Coolworld refrigeration component; staff caught it in time and no blood products were lost. Follows similar supermarket fridge attacks across France, Belgium and the Netherlands.

action: Patch/replace Zyxel GS1900 switches (CVE-2026-107441); apply Cisco's updated Node2Shell advisory (CVE-2026-111497) across all affected Cisco/Splunk products; patch Barracuda ESG and related products (CVE-2026-116606, CVE-2026-111560); update OpenSSH to 10.6p2 on Alpine/musl systems. Chainalysis customers and users of WorkOS, Northflank, Trigger.dev and Chainstack should rotate credentials and API keys immediately.
